requirement: Write down the scope boundary: which business units, networks and locations are in, and agree it with the assessor before starting.
evidence_examples: Scope statement; network diagram; list of sites in scope; assessor agreement
common_failure: Scope is vague, or quietly leaves out a site or network that users actually work on.

requirement: Include every end-user device that can reach organisational data or services. A scope that leaves out user devices is not acceptable.
evidence_examples: Device list by user group; MDM enrolment report
common_failure: Phones or tablets that read company email are left off the list.

requirement: Keep an up-to-date inventory of in-scope devices (servers, user devices, firewalls, routers) showing owner, operating system and support status.
evidence_examples: Asset register export; MDM or endpoint management report; last-seen dates
common_failure: Inventory is a spreadsheet nobody has updated since the last audit, so the assessor finds devices that are not on it.

requirement: List every cloud service that holds or processes organisational data, who is responsible for each control (you or the provider), and keep all of them in scope.
evidence_examples: Cloud service register; provider security statements; admin role list per service
common_failure: Shadow or free-tier services are missing from the register, or a service is declared out of scope.

requirement: Decide whether personal devices (BYOD) may access organisational data. Those that do are in scope; keep a list or block them.
evidence_examples: BYOD policy; conditional access rules; list of registered personal devices
common_failure: A BYOD policy exists on paper but nothing technical stops unregistered personal devices connecting.

requirement: Cover home and remote working: devices used at home are in scope, and a router supplied by the organisation is in scope.
evidence_examples: Remote working policy; software firewall setting evidence; list of supplied routers
common_failure: Remote devices rely on a home router the organisation does not control and have no software firewall.

requirement: If anything is excluded, justify the exclusion, explain how it is separated from the rest, and list every legal entity that is in scope.
evidence_examples: Exclusion register; segregation evidence (firewall or VLAN rules); entity list with company numbers
common_failure: A subsidiary or site is excluded but shares a flat network with in-scope systems.

requirement: Bring accounts used by suppliers, contractors and managed service providers into scope, and any organisation-owned device lent to a third party.
evidence_examples: Third-party account register; supplier access agreements; loaned device list
common_failure: Supplier admin accounts share one login and have no MFA.

requirement: Protect every in-scope device with a correctly configured firewall: a boundary firewall, or a firewall on the device itself.
applies_to: All in-scope devices and cloud services
evidence_examples: Firewall configuration export; host firewall policy report
common_failure: A site has an ISP router only, with unknown configuration, and devices have no host firewall.

requirement: Change the default administrator password on firewalls and routers to a strong, unique one, or switch remote administration off.
evidence_examples: Device configuration screenshot; password vault record; change log
common_failure: A branch router still has the manufacturer's default login.

requirement: Do not expose firewall administration pages to the internet unless there is a documented business need and either MFA or an allow list of trusted addresses is in place.
evidence_examples: External scan result; firewall admin access rules; documented business need
common_failure: A management interface is reachable from anywhere on the internet with a password only.

requirement: Block unauthenticated inbound connections by default and only open what is needed.
evidence_examples: Inbound rule set with default deny; external port scan
common_failure: Old remote desktop or database ports are open to the internet.

requirement: Have each inbound rule approved and documented by an authorised person, with the business reason recorded.
evidence_examples: Firewall change records; rule register with approver and reason
common_failure: Rules exist with no owner, no reason and no approval trail.

requirement: Remove or disable inbound rules as soon as they are no longer needed.
evidence_examples: Periodic rule review record; change tickets that close rules
common_failure: Temporary rules for a project or supplier stay open for years.

requirement: Run a software firewall on devices that are used on untrusted networks such as home or public Wi-Fi.
evidence_examples: Endpoint firewall policy; compliance report showing firewall enabled
common_failure: Firewall is turned off on some laptops for convenience or because of an old application.

requirement: For cloud services, use the provider's network and data flow controls (for example access rules and allow lists) where a firewall cannot be used.
evidence_examples: Security group or network rule export; tenant access restriction settings
common_failure: Cloud storage or databases left open to the internet by default settings.

requirement: Regularly remove or disable accounts that are not needed, including guest, default and unused administrator accounts.
applies_to: All in-scope devices and cloud services
evidence_examples: Account review record; directory report of disabled and stale accounts
common_failure: Former staff or test accounts are still enabled, or the built-in administrator account is active.

requirement: Change default or easily guessed passwords on every device and application.
applies_to: All in-scope devices and cloud services
evidence_examples: Build checklist; password vault records; scan for default credentials
common_failure: Printers, cameras, network switches and appliances still use factory passwords.

requirement: Remove or disable software, utilities and network services that are not needed.
evidence_examples: Standard build list; software inventory against approved list; service review
common_failure: Trial software, old remote tools and unused server roles remain installed.

requirement: Turn off auto-run features that start files without the user choosing to.
evidence_examples: Group policy or MDM setting; configuration report
common_failure: Auto-run is still on for removable media on older builds.

requirement: Make sure users are authenticated before they can reach organisational data or services.
applies_to: All in-scope devices and cloud services
evidence_examples: Sign-in policy; list of services requiring authentication; conditional access rules
common_failure: Shared drives or web apps are reachable without signing in.

requirement: Lock devices: require a password, PIN or biometric to unlock, and limit repeated guessing (for example no more than 10 attempts, or throttling).
evidence_examples: Screen lock and passcode policy; compliance report; lockout setting
common_failure: Phones have no passcode, or the unlock PIN is shorter than the minimum.

requirement: Make sure all in-scope software is licensed and still supported by its vendor.
evidence_examples: Software inventory with support end dates; licence records
common_failure: Old operating systems, firmware or applications past end of support are still in use.

requirement: Remove software that has gone out of support, or take the device out of scope using a separated network sub-set that has no internet access.
evidence_examples: Removal records; segregation evidence for any isolated sub-set
common_failure: A legacy machine is declared isolated but still has a route to the internet.

requirement: Turn on automatic updates wherever the product offers them.
evidence_examples: Update policy or ring configuration; settings screenshots
common_failure: Auto-update is disabled for applications such as browsers or PDF readers.

requirement: Install operating system and firmware updates within 14 days of release when they fix vulnerabilities rated critical or high, scored 7 or more on CVSS v3, or have no severity given.
applies_to: Operating systems, router and firewall firmware
evidence_examples: Patch compliance report with release and install dates; firmware change records
common_failure: Router and firewall firmware is left alone for months, or laptops that are rarely online miss the window.

requirement: Install application updates, including browser extensions and plug-ins, within 14 days of release under the same severity rules.
evidence_examples: Application patch report; third-party patching tool output
common_failure: Third-party applications and browser extensions are not covered by the patching tool.

requirement: If an update bundles several fixes and any one is critical or high, install the whole bundle within 14 days.
evidence_examples: Update approval records showing whole bundles installed
common_failure: Only the individual high fix is applied and the rest of the cumulative update is deferred.

requirement: Practical measure: be able to show which in-scope devices are missing critical or high updates older than 14 days, including devices that are offline.
applies_to: Servers, desktops, laptops, tablets, phones, firewalls
evidence_examples: Patch status dashboard; vulnerability scan report; offline device report
common_failure: Nobody can say how many devices are behind, so gaps are found by the assessor first.

requirement: Have a process to request, approve and create user accounts.
evidence_examples: Joiner process; approval records; account creation tickets
common_failure: Accounts are created on request by email with no approval record.

requirement: Give each person unique credentials before they can use applications or devices; avoid shared accounts.
evidence_examples: Directory export showing named accounts; shared account exceptions with controls
common_failure: A shared login is used for a machine, a shared mailbox or a supplier portal.

requirement: Remove or disable accounts when they are no longer needed, for example when someone leaves or after a set period of inactivity.
evidence_examples: Leaver checklist; stale account report; disablement dates against leaving dates
common_failure: Leaver accounts remain active for weeks because HR and IT are not connected.

requirement: Turn on MFA for every cloud service that offers it, whether the option is free, bundled or paid.
evidence_examples: MFA enforcement settings per service; sign-in report showing MFA coverage; list of services with no MFA option
common_failure: A service offers MFA but it is not enforced, or guest, service and unapproved accounts are skipped.

requirement: Require MFA on administrator accounts and on any account that can be reached from the internet.
evidence_examples: Admin role list with MFA status; remote access MFA configuration
common_failure: Admins use MFA for the portal but not for remote access or a second tenant.

requirement: Use separate administrator accounts for administration only, never for email, web browsing or everyday work.
evidence_examples: Admin account naming and list; mailbox licence report; browsing policy for admin accounts
common_failure: IT staff read email and browse the web with their administrator login.

requirement: Take away special privileges when they are no longer needed, for example after a change of role.
evidence_examples: Privileged access review; role change records
common_failure: Privileges accumulate as people move between roles.

requirement: Where passwords are used, protect against guessing with MFA, throttling (no more than 10 guesses in 5 minutes) or lockout after no more than 10 failures.
evidence_examples: Lockout or throttling settings per system
common_failure: Externally reachable sign-ins have no lockout or throttling.

requirement: Apply a password quality control: MFA, or at least 12 characters, or at least 8 characters with common passwords blocked.
evidence_examples: Password policy settings; banned password list configuration
common_failure: Minimum length is 8 and nothing blocks common passwords.

requirement: Help people choose unique passwords, for example by providing a password manager and guidance on long passphrases, and do not force routine expiry.
evidence_examples: Password manager rollout; staff guidance; password policy without forced expiry
common_failure: Staff reuse passwords because there is no approved way to store them.

requirement: Have a process to change passwords promptly when a compromise is known or suspected.
evidence_examples: Incident procedure covering credential compromise; reset records
common_failure: No documented way to force a reset quickly across systems.

requirement: Apply the same account controls to third-party accounts such as support and managed service provider logins.
evidence_examples: Supplier account list with MFA and approval evidence
common_failure: Supplier accounts are exempt from MFA and leaver processes.

requirement: Have a malware protection method active on every in-scope device.
applies_to: All in-scope devices and cloud services
evidence_examples: Endpoint protection coverage report; list of devices using allow listing
common_failure: Servers, unmanaged devices or specialist machines have no protection.

requirement: If using anti-malware software, keep it updated, make sure it stops malware running, and make it block known malicious websites.
applies_to: Windows and macOS servers, desktops, laptops
evidence_examples: Console report of version and signature currency; web protection setting
common_failure: Protection is installed but out of date, or web protection is off.

requirement: If using application allow listing, only approved, validly signed applications may run, the approved list is kept current, and users cannot install unsigned ones.
evidence_examples: Allow list policy export; approval process; store restriction settings
common_failure: Users can install software from outside the approved source.

requirement: Practical measure: check regularly that protection is present and current on every device, including new builds and laptops that are rarely online.
evidence_examples: Weekly coverage report; exception list with owners
common_failure: New devices go into use before protection is installed.
